<reason>A won by holding the motion as written and making the clash easier to decide. Specific-concern monitoring is not waiting for a body; B’s default package (especially always-on message reading) could not survive B’s own “not where intimacy lives” line. A split ordinary tools (curfews, empty-house check-ins) from standing custody of speech, and showed B’s hardest cases either already authorize looking or are designed to look normal, so the dashboard fails its own justification. B kept a live detection-paradox and irreversibility weighing, but paid for converting every friend thread into an undiagnosed emergency.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Q1/R2 turn of B’s “lethal third parties, not intimacy” into a contradiction: always-on reading of ordinary friend chats, plus the follow that grooming-that-looks-normal also defeats the feed.</best_rebuttal>
